title: Weekly time-series bins for topic-trends
description:
## Context
`analyze topic-trends` (src `topic_trends.py`, docs `topic-modeling.md`) reports momentum per topic over trailing windows (`30d`, `90d`, `1y`, `all`). Consumers that draw sparklines and trend charts need a per-topic series binned by calendar week instead. The documents already carry `dates.published_at`, so this is counting on dates that are already loaded.

Papyrus consumer: PPY-428252 (public knowledge base initiative). Related Biblicus items: blbs-d380cb (parent epic).

As a publication builder, I want a weekly count series per topic, so that a front end can draw an 8-week sparkline and a 26-week chart.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Weekly bins for topic trends
  Scenario: Request weekly bins
    Given a corpus whose items have published dates across ten weeks
    When I run topic-trends with weekly binning for the last 8 weeks
    Then each topic reports exactly 8 integer counts ordered oldest to newest
    And weeks are ISO weeks and the final bin is the current week

  Scenario: Items without a published date
    Given items with no published date
    When I run topic-trends with weekly binning
    Then those items are excluded from every bin and counted in a reported "undated" total

  Scenario: Existing trailing windows unchanged
    When I run topic-trends without a binning option
    Then the output is identical to the current trailing-window output
```

## Out of scope
Per-entity series (counted in Papyrus over confirmed entity links, see PPY-428252). Cluster identity (see the cluster-identity story under blbs-d380cb).
